questions.solution: Factoring $(x^2 - 60)(x^2 - 4) = 0$ with $60 \neq 4 > 0$ yields $4$ distinct real roots $\pm\sqrt{60}, \pm\sqrt{4}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If the equations $x^2 - 62x + 61 = 0$ and $x^2 - 6x + k = 0$ share the common root $x = 1$, find the value of $k$.
questions.solution: Substituting the common root $x = 1$ into the second equation gives $1 - (6) + k = 0 \implies k = 5$.
questions.explanation: Apply common roots & parameter elimination techniques in Trigonometry (Trigonometric Equations General Solutions).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If the equations $2x^2 + 124x + 12 = 0$ and $x^2 + p x + q = 0$ have both roots in common, find the value of $p + q$.
questions.solution: Proportionality of coefficients $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{p}{124} = \frac{q}{12} \implies p = 62,\; q = 6 \implies p + q = 68$.
questions.explanation: Apply common roots & parameter elimination techniques in Trigonometry (Principal Value of Inverse Trig).

questions.question: Find the largest integral value of $m$ for which the number $x = 7$ lies strictly between the two real roots of $f(x) = x^2 - 14x + m = 0$.
questions.solution: For $x = 7$ to lie strictly between the roots, $f(7) < 0 \implies 7^2 - 2(7^2) + m < 0 \implies m < 49$, so largest integer is $48$.
questions.explanation: Apply location of roots on real axis techniques in Trigonometry (Conditional Identities in Triangle).
tags: Location of Roots on Real Axis
